title: Girdermark parts data sheets: neutralize eight mixed-light bench product shots to an in-frame grey card, recolor a safety-orange fixture to a graphite colorway without a reshoot, prep-and-vectorize the wordmark, then data-merge one press-ready product data sheet per SKU

source.reference: Catalog designer needed — B2B electrical/elevator parts distributor (per-SKU product data sheets)

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief for a B2B wholesale distributor of electrical and elevator replacement parts that sells to service technicians, maintenance supervisors, and electrical contractors and wanted distributor-facing product material with clean product photography, complete specs and pricing for every part. Laundered to the fictional brand 'Girdermark Elevator & Electrical Supply' — no real company, person, product, or trademark is named anywhere (the earlier 'Ironclad' laundering was dropped because the bare word collides with an unrelated real SaaS firm). REPOSITIONED for connector reality and to SHIP THE CATALOG rather than merely audit it (the prior version of this slot was a report-only 'pre-press audit' that produced only a findings CSV/txt — killed as a non-designed, defect-list-in-the-brief analyze task). The original brief implied a ~100-page multi-up catalog, which is NOT connector-doable: document_merge_data_layout emits exactly ONE FILE PER ROW and cannot place several records on one page, and a convert_pdf_to_indd template will not bind merge fields. So the client is modeled as needing what the merge tool genuinely produces — a per-SKU PRODUCT DATA SHEET (one US Letter single-record sell/spec sheet per part) for the distributor binder and the field-PDF. The client supplies a genuinely hand-authored InDesign single-record data-sheet template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> and TWO @-prefixed image-path columns (one for the product photo, one for the masthead wordmark), the parts roster as a CSV, eight raw product photos shot on the bench across two sessions under mismatched light each with a photographic 18% grey card laid in frame, and a flat wordmark scan on off-white stock. The Adobe chain does the real work the brief rewards: neutralize every bench shot to its own in-frame grey card so the whole set shares one white point and prints sharp, isolate each part onto a clean solid-white catalog background, recolor a safety-orange emergency-fixture line to a graphite colorway so the client can preview the variant without a reshoot, prep-and-vectorize the scanned wordmark, then run the authored template through a one-file-per-row data-merge and export one press-ready product data sheet per SKU.
one_line_ask: Bring our eight bench product photos — shot on two different days under whatever light was on the bench, each with a grey card in the corner — to one consistent, print-sharp catalog look by neutralizing each to its own grey card, lift every part cleanly onto a solid-white catalog background, show our safety-orange emergency push-button in a graphite colorway without reshooting it, get our wordmark scan into razor-sharp vector for the sheet masthead, then merge the parts roster into our authored InDesign data-sheet template so every SKU gets its own press-ready product data sheet.
full_brief: Girdermark Elevator & Electrical Supply is a wholesale distributor of electrical and elevator replacement parts selling to service technicians, maintenance supervisors, and electrical contractors. Our buyers open this material in the field — often as a phone PDF — when they need to spec a replacement part fast and prepare a quote, so a sheet that looks cheap or a part they can't see clearly costs us an order. We are relaunching our line and need the production done: one clean, consistent product data sheet per part for the distributor binder, each carrying the part's number, description, voltage, amperage, list price and section alongside a sharp product photo, with our wordmark crisp at the top. We are NOT reshooting. Here is the problem with the photos: we handed the bench to two different people on two mornings, and they shot under whatever light was there — some under cool LED bench lamps, some under warm tungsten work lights, a couple under- or over-exposed — so straight out of the folder the eight shots look like a mismatched jumble, and a binder of mismatched shots reads amateur to a contractor. To make this checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card into the corner of every shot. Your job on the photos: bring every image to one consistent, true-to-part look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set will share one white point. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance and exposure decision to land on the shared target — some need warming, others cooling, and pushing one set of numbers through all of them will leave the set mismatched. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame and the final pixel size of each, so we can confirm the set is genuinely matched and that every part will still be sharp at print size: each sheet drops the photo into a 5 x 4 inch product window, and at press resolution that window needs at least ~1500 x 1200 px of real image — a part cropped down to a small web thumbnail will print soft and we will reject it. Second, lift each part cleanly off its cluttered bench and set it on a pure solid-white catalog background with the bench and the grey card gone — the way a distributor catalog shows a part; just the part on white, no messy bench, and the black travel-cable coil is the hard one because it was shot on a dark bench and nearly disappears into it, so isolate it by what it IS, not by brightness. Third, a colorway without a reshoot: our emergency push-button fixture is safety-orange, but we are considering a graphite line and want to see it — give us a version of that same shot with the orange housing turned a deep gunmetal graphite (drained of its orange and darkened, staying a believable metal, NOT a flat painted-on grey), and the recolor has to sit under the real moulding, sheen and shadow of the housing, touching only the housing and not the button, the bezel, or the bench. Fourth, our wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper — get it clean and razor-sharp for the sheet masthead so it does not look like a fuzzy scan when printed. Finally, build the sheets: we have hand-built the InDesign data-sheet template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (one for the product photo, one for the wordmark at the top), and we are giving you the parts roster; merge them so every SKU gets its own single-page sheet with its part number, description, voltage, amperage, price and section bound in, its matching isolated photo dropped in, and the crisp wordmark in the masthead — then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF, one page per SKU. Bind the part data verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite our specs or prices, and some part numbers are long and must fit the auto-size code frame without clipping. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set on one white point; every product photo at least ~1500 x 1200 px so it prints >=300 DPI in the 5 x 4 window; the graphite recolor confined to the housing and natural under the real light; the wordmark a clean skew-free vector; and exactly one finished data sheet per roster row.

inputs.name: girdermark_datasheet_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US Letter (8.5x11) portrait product data sheet — ONE part per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<part_no>>, <<description>>, <<voltage>>, <<amperage>>, <<list_price>>, <<section>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a 5 x 4 inch product image frame bound to @Photo (the matching isolated part photo), and a masthead image frame bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized Girdermark wordmark). CRITICAL masthead geometry: the template carries a PURE-WHITE masthead strip running across the very top edge of the sheet, and the @Wordmark image frame sits ENTIRELY inside that white strip — this white strip is a SEPARATE band that sits ABOVE and is DISTINCT FROM the fixed navy header band beneath it. The @Wordmark frame never overlaps the navy band. Because the navy wordmark's vectorized enclosed counters are crisped to white, they can only read correctly on a light ground, so the mark is bound onto the WHITE masthead strip (counters invisible against white = correct) and NO dark-ground knockout is claimed anywhere. The <<part_no>> text frame has Auto-Size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so long alphanumeric part codes bind without going overset/clipped. The white masthead strip (top), the navy header band (directly below it), the footer and the section-label rule are already drawn into the template artwork (fixed on every sheet), so the only per-row imagery is the product photo and the wordmark. Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark reaches the masthead ONLY as a merge bind through the second image frame — it is not dropped in by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-up grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-record catalog page would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record data sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape (this is the fix for the killed multi-up catalog / audit-only concept). Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. TWO image columns (@Photo, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's isolated part photo AND the shared vectorized wordmark — so the chain-produced wordmark has a real, connector-doable path onto every sheet without any free-form placement. The auto-size code frame resolves the old overset defect: long codes now bind cleanly instead of clipping.

inputs.name: girdermark_parts_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns exactly part_no,description,voltage,amperage,list_price,section,@Photo,@Wordmark holding 8 electrical/elevator parts rows, one per SKU, distributed across five sections: 'Contactors & Relays' (3-pole contactor), 'Elevator Door Operators' (door operator motor unit), 'Push-Button Fixtures' (safety-orange emergency push-button AND a brass floor-indicator bezel), 'Fuses & Breakers' (cartridge fuse set AND a miniature circuit breaker), 'Cables & Connectors' (coiled travel cable AND a crimp connector kit). Use realistic industrial part numbers with a mix of SHORT and DELIBERATELY LONG alphanumeric codes (e.g. 'CR-40' vs 'GRM-DOL-CONTACTOR-40A-3P-24VDC-COIL-AUX-2NO2NC') so the template's shrink-to-fit code frame is exercised; voltages like '24VDC'/'120VAC'/'480VAC', amperage like '10A'/'40A', US-dollar prices like '$28.40'. Each row carries a keyword-rich one-to-two-line B2B product description. The @Photo column names the matching isolated packshot filename for that SKU in row order (photo_p1_final.jpg ... photo_p8_final.jpg) so the [T] merge drops each isolated photo into that row's single-record sheet. The @Wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — girdermark_wordmark.svg — in EVERY row, so the merge drops the one shared masthead mark onto every sheet as a merge bind (never free-form placement). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<part_no>>,<<description>>,<<voltage>>,<<amperage>>,<<list_price>>,<<section>> and the two @image-path columns @Photo and @Wordmark.
inputs.realism_notes: Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight finished sheets (page-count = row-count gate). Headers match the authored .indd fields and BOTH @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the correct photo, AND the shared wordmark per SKU. @Wordmark carries the identical vectorized SVG path in all eight rows, giving the chain-produced wordmark a connector-doable path onto every sheet via the merge (mirrors AO-74/AO-75's two-image-column pattern). The @Photo filenames are the exact names the agent must produce and upload, so naming discipline is a real dependency. The mix of short/long part codes exercises the auto-fit frame; specs bind verbatim (no rewriting).

inputs.name: raw_bench_product_photos_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera captures of electrical/elevator replacement parts laid on a workshop bench, each ~3500-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera, roughly 4000x3000 or larger before crop), each with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference. Shot across two mornings under mismatched light: (1) a black/dark-grey 3-pole contactor, cool bluish LED bench-lamp cast, slightly under-exposed, frame tilted ~3 deg; (2) an elevator door-operator motor unit (grey painted housing), warm tungsten work-light cast, slightly bright; (3) a SAFETY-ORANGE emergency push-button fixture (bright orange housing, black button, chrome bezel), warm tungsten cast — this is the recolor hero; (4) a polished BRASS elevator floor-indicator bezel that is GENUINELY warm gold, shot under near-neutral daylight so its grey card ALREADY reads neutral (the gold is the real finish, not a white-balance error); (5) a set of cartridge fuses on a tray, cool LED cast, under-exposed, frame tilted ~4 deg; (6) a miniature circuit breaker (white/grey body), warm tungsten cast, OVER-exposed with hot highlights on the casing; (7) a coiled black elevator travel cable shot ON A DARK BENCH so it nearly merges into the background (low fabric-to-background contrast), cool cast; (8) a crimp-connector kit (mixed metal lugs), near-neutral but flat/low-contrast light, frame tilted ~2 deg. Every shot has real material texture (moulded plastic, brushed metal, cable jacket), cluttered workshop-bench surroundings, candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI. The grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in each.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~3500-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each product crop can fill the 5 x 4 inch data-sheet window at ~300 DPI (>=1500 x 1200 px) by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere in the chain. Deliberately mismatched (per-frame WB, exposure, and tilt vary in opposite directions) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own decision measured to its in-frame 18% grey card. Photo 4 is the UNDISCLOSED trap: its warmth is the real brass finish and its card is already neutral, so any batch 'warm the cool cast' or 'cool an imagined warm cast' move strips the real gold — the brief never flags this frame. Photo 3 carries the safety-orange housing for the masked graphite recolor. Photo 7 is the hardest isolation edge (black cable on a dark bench). Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs; the grey card is cropped out of the final packshot.

inputs.name: girdermark_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'GIRDERMARK' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: a bold industrial condensed sans-serif in solid navy with a small elevator-rail-and-lightning-bolt glyph to the left, no gradients. Rendered as a scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole thing sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around the mark, and edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, boost contrast/crispness, crop to the mark, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. Flat solid-navy two-colour mark on a LIGHT ground so the trace keeps clean edges and the glyph's enclosed counters read as white (no dark-ground knockout claimed). gemini-3-pro-image chosen because the mark carries legible type.

outputs.name: Girdermark_ProductDataSheets_perSKU_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready US Letter (8.5x11) portrait product data sheets — ONE single-record sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each sheet binds its part_no/description/voltage/amperage/list_price/section verbatim from the roster (long part codes shrink-to-fit without clipping) with its matching grey-card-neutralized, isolated-on-white product photo dropped into the 5 x 4 inch product frame (via @Photo, >=1500 x 1200 px so it prints >=300 DPI) and the vectorized wordmark dropped into the masthead frame (via @Wordmark) — both by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality. The safety-orange push-button sheet shows the part in its true orange (its real color); the graphite recolor is a separate preview deliverable, not a merged page.

outputs.name: packshots_isolated_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized parts photos isolated onto a pure solid-white catalog background (#FFFFFF), delivered as the product-framed crops (grey card and bench cropped/removed) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-isolation neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, decoupled claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-isolation neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point while staying true-to-part (no part's real finish forced off — the brass bezel stays gold, the orange housing stays orange); (b) card/bench-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered isolated packshot (the *_final output that binds into that SKU's sheet) — the part sits on solid white with no grey card and no bench pixels, and remove_background isolates the OUTER background only (no enclosed-hole knockout is required or claimed); (c) each packshot is >=1500 x 1200 px (>=300 DPI in the 5 x 4 window). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the isolated packshot. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move AND final pixel size applied to each frame.

outputs.name: variant_pushbutton_graphite.jpg
outputs.spec: Recolored colorway preview of the safety-orange emergency push-button hero: the orange housing turned a deep gunmetal graphite via a masked image_adjust_hsl pass pair — a strong orange-band DESATURATION plus a luminance drop that darkens the housing to a believable metal (an in-band desaturate-and-darken, the connector-doable safety-orange -> gunmetal move; NOT a near-complementary hue rotation) riding the housing's existing luminosity so its moulding, sheen highlights and cast shadow stay natural, and confined to the housing mask so the black button, the chrome bezel and the bench are untouched — no whole-image overlay, no flat dead-fill. Isolated onto solid white and sized to the catalog spec.

outputs.name: girdermark_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the Girdermark wordmark, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured off-white paper ground or skew; the glyph's enclosed counters (crisped to white) read clean because the mark binds onto the template's pure-white masthead strip, which is distinct from and above the fixed navy header band — no dark-ground knockout is claimed.

connector_workflow.note: Load the eight bench product photos, the wordmark scan, the authored .indd data-sheet template and the parts roster CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. (Single upload — plumbing, not counted as difficulty.)
Triage: this frame is tilted ~3 deg, so level it first. (Only the tilted frames 1/5/8 get straightened; the level frames skip this — deciding which is part of the job.)

SKU-1 contactor (Session A, cool LED cast, under-exposed): WARM the temperature (positive) and nudge tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then LIFT exposure to the shared brightness while holding the black point so the dark housing does not crush to pure black. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card — do NOT reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _brightness_and_contrast / _vibrance_and_saturation).

Isolate the contactor onto a solid-white catalog background via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) — this removes the cluttered bench AND the grey card in one correct move. This is the CORRECT knockout path (isolates the outer background, part as foreground); deliberately NOT select_subject->invert_selection->image_fill_area (select_subject is person-only and mis-fires on a bench part, and fill_area solids the whole mask). No enclosed-hole cut-out is claimed.

Crop/reframe the isolated contactor to the 5 x 4 (5:4) product-window ratio, keeping >=1500 x 1200 px so it clears the 300 DPI print floor. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand. The pre-isolation p1_neutralized master (grey card still in frame) is RETAINED as the neutrality-grading artifact; the card's neutrality is graded THERE, never on this packshot. Report final px. Feeds SKU-1's @Photo cell.

SKU-2 door-operator motor (Session B, warm tungsten, bright): this frame must move the OPPOSITE direction from frame 1 — COOL it (negative temperature) and pull exposure DOWN until its grey card reads neutral and it matches the shared white point. Adaptive: the batch is not uniformly cool, so a blanket 'warm everything' pass fails here. Report the move.
Isolate the door-operator unit onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); bench and grey card removed. Outer-background isolation only.
Crop to the 5:4 product window at >=1500 x 1200 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. Feeds SKU-2's @Photo cell.

SKU-3 safety-orange push-button (Session B, warm tungsten): COOL to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point, protecting the orange housing's real chroma (neutralize the LIGHT cast, do not desaturate the part here). This neutralized master feeds BOTH its own true-orange packshot AND the graphite recolor branch, so keep it before isolation. Report the move.

Isolate the true-orange push-button onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) for its own SKU-3 sheet (the sheet shows the part in its real orange). Outer-background isolation only.
Crop to the 5:4 product window at >=1500 x 1200 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. Feeds SKU-3's @Photo cell (true orange).

SKU-4 brass floor-indicator bezel — THE TRAP FRAME. The bezel is GENUINELY warm gold and it was shot under near-neutral daylight, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies the same 'warm the cool cast' correction used on frames 1/5/7, or that 'cools an imagined warm cast', will neutralize the card off-neutral and strip the real brass gold. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held.
Isolate the brass bezel onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); bench and grey card removed. Outer-background isolation only.
Crop to the 5:4 product window at >=1500 x 1200 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. Feeds SKU-4's @Photo cell (real gold held).
Tilted ~4 deg — level it.

SKU-5 cartridge fuse set (Session A, cool LED, under-exposed): warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point and LIFT exposure to the set brightness. Distinct numbers from frame 1 because the light differed. Report the move.
Isolate the fuse tray onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); bench and grey card removed.
Crop to the 5:4 product window at >=1500 x 1200 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. Feeds SKU-5's @Photo cell.

SKU-6 miniature circuit breaker (Session B, warm, OVER-exposed): PULL exposure/highlights/whites DOWN first to recover the blown white casing, THEN cool a touch so its grey card lands neutral on the shared white point. Tonal recovery dominates here — opposite tonal direction from the under-exposed frames 1/5. Report the move.
Isolate the circuit breaker onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); bench and grey card removed.
Crop to the 5:4 product window at >=1500 x 1200 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. Feeds SKU-6's @Photo cell.

SKU-7 coiled black travel cable (Session A, cool, shot on a DARK bench): warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point and hold shadow detail in the black jacket without lifting it to grey. Report the move.

Isolate the black cable coil onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) — the HARDEST edge in the batch because the black jacket sits on a dark bench at near-identical luminance; the semantic foreground isolation (not a brightness/luminance guess, and NOT select_subject->invert->fill_area) is what makes this survivable. Bench and grey card removed.
Crop to the 5:4 product window at >=1500 x 1200 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. Feeds SKU-7's @Photo cell.
Tilted ~2 deg — level it.

SKU-8 crimp-connector kit (near-neutral but flat/low-contrast): its grey card is already close to neutral, so only a SMALL WB nudge is needed to sit on the shared white point — over-correcting would push it off the set. The real work is tonal: add contrast/clarity to match the set's feel without clipping. Report the (small WB, tonal) move. Frames 1-8 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.
Isolate the crimp-connector kit onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); bench and grey card removed.
Crop to the 5:4 product window at >=1500 x 1200 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. Feeds SKU-8's @Photo cell.

Recolor branch (from the neutralized orange hero): semantically select ONLY the safety-orange push-button housing ('the orange plastic emergency push-button housing'), excluding the black button, the chrome bezel and the bench, so the graphite recolor is confined to the part. Returns a maskURI. Not a hue/coordinate selection — a real object/part.

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes hero + housing mask): drain the orange — a strong DESATURATION of the orange band together with a luminance drop that darkens the housing toward gunmetal, letting the housing's existing luminosity carry the moulding, sheen highlights and cast shadow. This is the connector-doable safety-orange -> gunmetal/graphite move (a desaturate-and-darken within band; NOT a near-complementary hue rotation, which image_adjust_hsl cannot control). Confined to the mask. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the button, bezel and bench) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (kills the moulded sheen) — both wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): settle the luminance and trim any residual orange-band chroma so the housing lands on a believable deep graphite metal instead of a flat dead grey or a still-warm brown, still riding the original luminosity so the moulding and shadow stay natural. A deepen-and-neutralize in the same band, not a swing to a new hue.
Isolate the graphite-recolored push-button onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) to match the catalog look; bench and grey card removed. Outer-background isolation only.
Crop/resize the finished graphite colorway preview to the catalog spec (>=1500 x 1200 px). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Separate preview deliverable — NOT a merged sheet page.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the off-white paper toward white so the navy lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). Light ground, so the glyph's enclosed counters read clean.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: girdermark_datasheet_template.indd, girdermark_parts_roster.csv, photo_p1_final, photo_p2_final, photo_p3_final, photo_p4_final, photo_p5_final, photo_p6_final, photo_p7_final, photo_p8_final, girdermark_wordmark.svg
connector_workflow.note: One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight roster rows (part_no/description/voltage/amperage/list_price/section) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve BOTH image columns per row — drop that row's isolated photo into the @Photo product frame AND the vectorized wordmark (from @Wordmark, the same SVG in every row) into the masthead frame — producing EXACTLY ONE merged sheet per row (eight sheets); the auto-fit code frame shrinks long part numbers so they bind without clipping. Binding the wordmark through the @Wordmark image column is the ONLY connector-doable path onto the sheet (free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned). [T] requires the hand-authored template with its two merge-wired image frames. A multi-up catalog page or a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind / cannot be produced — this is the corrected merge path that ships the catalog. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool (text-only, cannot bind @Photo/@Wordmark).

Export the merged single-record sheets to a press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter portrait PDF, one sheet per SKU. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all eight sheets, one page per SKU) in a single call — it cannot export one named record on its own, so no per-record named export is attempted. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout.
